articles.title: The report complicates Vinicius's presence in the Clásico: "Aggressive attitude" and protests "at the top of his voice"
articles.standfirst: The referee described the Brazilian's "aggressive attitude" when protesting his sending-off for the hair pull, an account that points to a suspension that could rule him out of the clash against Barça
articles.summary: The referee described the Brazilian's "aggressive attitude" when protesting his sending-off for the hair pull, an account that points to a suspension that could rule him out of the clash against Barça
articles.body:
"The referee's report for the match between Real Madrid and Villarreal (1-0), played this Saturday at the Santiago Bernabéu, detailed the sending-off of Vinicius Júnior and the subsequent protests by the Brazilian forward. The match official, Díaz de Mera, recorded in the document both the reason for the red card and an additional incident after the player had already been sent off.

Regarding the card, the report explained that Vinicius was sent off in the 73rd minute “for pulling an opponent’s hair, with the ball in play, without the ball being contested between them” . The incident occurred in the play in which the Brazilian had sent the ball into the net, in a goal that the referee disallowed after spotting that prior infringement.

The referee added a section on “other incidents” in which he described what happened after the sending-off. “In the 73rd minute of the match, with play stopped, the local club’s number 7 player, D. Vinicius José De Oliveira Do Nascimento, after having been sent off and while still on the field of play, continued protesting my decision, shouting at the top of his voice, moving toward the area where I was with an aggressive attitude,” Díaz de Mera wrote.

After having been sent off and while still on the field of play, he continued protesting my decision, shouting at the top of his voice, heading toward the area where I was with an aggressive attitude

The referee also specified that the forward “had to be restrained by teammates” , although he clarified that he could not “make out any specific expression.” The account in the match report, together with the CTA protocol, suggests that the suspension could go beyond a single match and, therefore, Vinicius would miss the Clásico against Barcelona next October 25 . Madrid only plays one league match in between, against Sevilla , so a ban of two or more matches would leave the Brazilian out of the appointment at Camp Nou.

The report was not limited to Vinicius. The referee also showed a caution to José Mourinho and delegate Chendo , and sent off Real Madrid's goalkeeping coach, Nuno Santos , on a night of maximum tension on the white team's bench over the refereeing decisions. For Villarreal, the official sent off Xisco Nadal , Villarreal delegate.

The CTA protocol includes hair-pulling within category CV.1, that of violent conduct, which groups together actions in which a “player delivers an elbow, headbutt, punch, slap, grab by the neck, shove, kick, stomp, bite, hair pull… to an opponent or any other person without contesting the ball, using excessive force or brutality” . This type of action for violent conduct usually carries a suspension of more than one match , a punishment that would leave the Brazilian out of El Clásico against Barcelona, since in between Madrid only plays the league match against Sevilla.

articles.title: Ex-Barcelona president blasts Messi: "Who does he think he is? He should be careful..."
articles.standfirst: The former Barcelona president demands that the Rosario star say goodbye to the blaugrana fans without making his return conditional on Joan Laporta’s presence
articles.summary: The former Barcelona president demands that the Rosario star say goodbye to the blaugrana fans without making his return conditional on Joan Laporta’s presence
articles.body:
'J oan Gaspart has spoken out again about Leo Messi and did so with a forceful message on the podcast "Solo Para Culés." The former Barcelona president spoke about the Argentine's possible farewell at Camp Nou and made it clear that, in his view, the player should return to say goodbye to the fans regardless of who holds the club's presidency.'

Gaspart maintains a special bond with Messi, since he was Barça's president when the Argentine arrived at the club at just 13 years old . Precisely because of that relationship, he wanted to make it clear that his words do not call into question the importance of the number 10 in the club's history.

"I say this from the historical love I have for a player whom I signed when he was 13 years old and I was the president of Barça ," Gaspart explained during the podcast. However, the former executive believes that Messi should not place his personal circumstances above the institution. "He should be careful. Barça is above him," he stated.

"Let him be careful, I say it from the long-standing love I have for a player I signed when he was 13 years old

One of the points he focused on was the relationship between Messi and Joan Laporta . Gaspart believes that the presence of the current president should not be an obstacle for the Argentine to return to Camp Nou and receive the fans' recognition.

' "Whoever the president is, let him come and say goodbye to Barça ," said the former blaugrana president, who was even more forceful when speaking about a possible tribute conditioned on Laporta's departure.'

"If Leo Messi comes to say goodbye and doesn't come because Laporta is the president and comes the day Laporta is no longer there, I would not go to that tribute ," he stated. Gaspart closed his remarks with a phrase that sums up his stance on the role Messi should have with regard to the club: "Who does he think he is?".

articles.title: The Villarreal goalkeeper was the victim of an armed robbery at his home while he and his family were inside
articles.standfirst: The Hungarian goalkeeper is out for the Champions clash against Napoli
articles.summary: The Hungarian goalkeeper is out for the Champions clash against Napoli
articles.body:
Villarreal goalkeeper Peter Gulacsi will be unavailable tonight for the match his team is set to play at La Cerámica against Napoli due to the severe emotional impact suffered after the armed robbery of which he has been the victim in the last few hours.

As the club from La Plana has reported, the footballer suffered an armed robbery during the early hours of this morning while he was at home with his family . The yellow club has reported that, fortunately, no member of his family was injured. The emotional impact has been such that the player is not in condition to play in a match like the one the yellows are playing tonight against Napoli

Peter Gulacsi, who arrived at Villarreal this summer, lives with his wife and his two young children , which gives a good idea of the impact that the scare they went through has had on the family.

This is not the first time that a similar incident has happened to a player from the yellow team. In previous seasons, players such as Toko Ekambi or Zambo Anguissa had already suffered similar situations. Also at Valencia, in previous campaigns, several footballers reported these incidents, such as Garay, Gabriel Paulista or Kondogbia.

articles.title: Mourinho asks the press to watch “the first minute of the Villarreal game, and then we'll talk”: What happened in that minute?
articles.standfirst: The coach dodged five questions about the refereeing controversy at the Bernabéu... and invited the press to look into what happened in the first minute of the match
articles.summary: The coach dodged five questions about the refereeing controversy at the Bernabéu... and invited the press to look into what happened in the first minute of the match
articles.body:
José Mourinho once again left an enigmatic message before the Spanish press. Asked repeatedly about the refereeing controversy during Madrid-Villarreal at the Bernabéu , the Portuguese coach avoided entering the debate and ended up inviting the Italian journalists to ask him about the match . Before that, Mou gave the Spanish press homework in order to understand his stance.

His answer, however, left a clue: "I invite you all to watch the first minute against Villarreal, just watch one minute, that's enough" . Mourinho went further and urged the press to return to the matter on Saturday, ahead of the league match: "For those who know, the first minute is enough" , he challenged the press at Rome's Olympic Stadium .

But, what exactly happened in that minute? The reference points to 1:04 of the match , a moment that takes on special relevance in light of his words. Upon reviewing the first five minutes, the only action that raises doubts is an offside given against Mbappé . Minutes later, the Frenchman was once again involved in a similar play... and the action ended the same way: offside against the French No. 10 .

MARCA has been able to confirm that Mourinho is referring to the first offside called on Mbappé. An action for which there was no replay during the broadcast, but which also did not generate any doubts on the pitch: the infringement was called and the match continued . No. 10 dropped deep to receive and, although the live review cannot confirm whether or not he was offside, the ball ended up in Villarreal's possession. A dubious offside in which the Frenchman had no chance of creating any kind of danger .

The key lies in the Portuguese coach's interpretation of that decision. Without being certain whether or not the forward was in an illegal position , Mourinho suggests that the refereeing predisposition was to call against Real Madrid . That is, at least, the reading the coach makes of a play he considers revealing enough to insist that it is enough to review the first minute of the match to understand what would end up happening afterward.

articles.title: A record-devouring Barcelona: and another could fall on Saturday
articles.standfirst: Would equal Madrid's 68/69 side with nine consecutive wins at the start of LaLiga
articles.summary: Would equal Madrid's 68/69 side with nine consecutive wins at the start of LaLiga
articles.body:
Barcelona's excellent run at the start of the season is allowing Flick's team to break record after record. Their goalscoring efficiency is overwhelming, with 43 goals scored in these ten matches. And this is where a new Champions League record comes in. In this competition, Barcelona have played 28 matches with Flick on the bench. In them they have scored a total of 84 goals, which amounts to an average of three goals per match. It is the highest scoring ratio of any team that has played at least twenty matches in this competition since the current format was established in the 1992-1993 season.

This Saturday another record could fall, although this time related to consecutive victories at the start of the league. The record is held by Real Madrid from the 1968-1969 season. The white team, then managed by Miguel Muñoz, achieved nine consecutive wins before drawing 0-0 on matchday ten against Pontevedra. At the moment, Barcelona has eight consecutive victories, so if they beat Betis at La Cartuja on Saturday, they will equal that mark.

On an individual level, Lamine Yamal doesn't stop . In the assists category, he has drawn level with Raphinha, with 13 since the youth academy graduate made his Champions League debut in September 2023. Since then, both have been the top assist providers, ahead of Vinicius, Dembélé, Achraf and Olise.

With yesterday's two assists, Lamine has already provided two in eight matches with Flick as coach. Half of them have come in matches played this season. Barcelona just keeps breaking records.

articles.title: Vinicius misses El Clásico: four-match ban
articles.standfirst: The Competition Committee imposes a harsh sanction on him for his red card against Villarreal
articles.summary: The Competition Committee imposes a harsh sanction on him for his red card against Villarreal
articles.body:
Vinicius will not be able to play in the Clásico as the Competition Committee has handed him a four-match suspension after seeing red in last Saturday's match against Villarreal . The Brazilian was sent off for pulling Nathan Saliba 's hair in the move that would end with his goal, which was later disallowed for this reason. He will miss the matches against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing and Valencia. He will not return until after the November international break.

The match official, Isidro Díaz de Mera, recorded in the match report both the reason for the red card and an additional incident with the player already sent off . It was the VAR who alerted the referee, who changed his mind after reviewing the play.

The report states the following: " 2-match suspension for acting violently off the play, with no possibility of contesting the ball or with play stopped , with additional fine(s) pursuant to Article 5. And another suspension: 2-match suspension for protesting to the referee, head referee, assistant referee, or fourth official".

' The fact that the ball was not in play has worked against the Brazilian in the sanction; otherwise it could have been just one match, but in addition the referee states in the report "aggressive attitude" on the part of the Madrid player and stresses that he had to be restrained by his teammates.'

Vinicius later apologized to his teammates and the fans for having left his team with ten men through social media. The player will miss the match against Sevilla next Sunday at 9:00 p.m. and the one at Camp Nou the following Sunday, October 25, at the same time. The forward was not in the starting lineup in the last match against Villarreal after returning from international duty, and his place was taken by Diomande.

The full disciplinary ruling

DE OLIVEIRA DO NASCIMENTO, VINICIUS JOSÉ "VINI JR." (Real Madrid CF) 2-match suspension for acting violently off the ball, with no possibility of contesting the ball or with play stopped, with additional fine(s) applied pursuant to article 52 of the Disciplinary Code. (Article: 130.2)

DE OLIVEIRA DO NASCIMENTO, VINICIUS JOSÉ "VINI JR." (Real Madrid CF ) 2-match suspension for protesting to the referee, head referee, assistant referee or fourth official, with additional fine(s) pursuant to Article 52 CD.. (Article: 127)

First. - Real Madrid Club de Fútbol states in its submission that there is a manifest material error, alleging that the images provided prove that the player did not actually pull his opponent's hair, but rather that there was accidental contact of his hand with the hair and headband the opponent was wearing, during a tussle between both footballers. Likewise, it argues that the action occurred during an ongoing play and that the footballer had the possibility of challenging for the ball, as would be shown by his subsequent involvement in the move that ended in a goal. Finally, with regard to the conduct after the sending-off, the Club maintains that the player's protests cannot constitute an autonomous infringement or justify an aggravation of the sanction.

Second. - It is a repeated criterion of this Disciplinary Committee that the finding of a manifest material error in the referee’s report requires the submission of evidence which unequivocally, beyond any reasonable doubt, proves either the non-existence of the fact recorded in the report or its evident arbitrariness. This repeated criterion is based on the following points: (i) First, Article 155 of the Competition Regulations of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF), which, in its first paragraph, establishes that “the referee is the sole and unappealable sporting authority, in technical matters, to officiate matches.” This same provision adds that among his obligations is that of “cautioning or sending off, depending on the seriousness of the offence, any footballer who displays incorrect conduct or behaves in an improper manner and likewise coaches, assistants and other persons affected under the regulations” (Article 156, paragraph 2, section e)); as well as that of “drawing up, faithfully, concisely, clearly, objectively and completely, the match report, as well as any supplementary reports he deems appropriate, sending both, with the utmost urgency and by the fastest procedure, to the competent entities and bodies” (Article 156, section b). Regarding the evidentiary value of these reports, Article 27 of the RFEF Disciplinary Code establishes that they “constitute necessary documentary evidence in the body of proof of infringements of sporting rules and regulations” (paragraph 1). And it adds that “in the assessment of infringements relating to sporting discipline, the referee’s decisions on facts related to play are final and presumed true, save for manifest material error” (paragraph 3). In this way, referees’ reports enjoy a rebuttable presumption of truthfulness, which may therefore be overturned when the existence of a manifest material error is proven. (ii) Second, the doctrine of the disciplinary bodies of this RFEF and of the Sports Administrative Court (TAD) supports the foregoing statements. All of them have clearly ruled in different decisions on the need for the evidence submitted to conclusively demonstrate the referee’s manifest error. In this regard, reference may be made to the TAD Decision of 29 September 2017 (Case 302/2017), which stated that “when the aforementioned Article 27 of the RFEF Disciplinary Code states that refereeing decisions on facts related to play are ‘final and presumed true, save for manifest material error,’ it is allowing the principle of immutability (‘final’) enjoyed by the refereeing decision in favor of legal certainty, in this case, of the Laws of the Game, nevertheless to be mitigated when there is a ‘manifest material error,’ as a modality or subspecies of ‘material error,’ that is, where there exists, as the Constitutional Court has indicated when referring to this term in procedural laws (See Articles 214.3 of the Civil Procedure Act and 267.3 of the Organic Law of the Judiciary), a clear or obvious error, independently of any opinion, assessment, interpretation or legal classification that may be made.” (iii) Lastly, from all of the above it follows that, in order to challenge the truthfulness of the decisions recorded in the referee’s report, the appellant must provide the disciplinary body with appropriate and sufficient evidence to demonstrate the existence of “a manifest material error.” In this regard, it is also settled doctrine of the TAD that declares the full validity of video evidence as a suitable evidentiary instrument to rebut the content of the referee’s report. For its part, it is incumbent upon the Disciplinary Committee to review and assess the content of the recording in order to verify whether or not it corresponds to the appellant’s allegations. In short, only proof of a manifest material error would rebut the presumption of truthfulness enjoyed by the referee’s report and would make it possible to set aside the caution under appeal.

Third. None of these circumstances are present, in the opinion of this Disciplinary Committee, in the case before us, since the appealing Club does not provide any evidence whatsoever capable of disproving what is stated in the referee’s report.

On the contrary, the images are compatible with the referee's account, making the hair pull unequivocal, and the considerations regarding the position of the hand, the arrangement of the fingers, or the supposedly accidental nature of the contact do not allow a manifest material error to be established under the terms required by article 27.3 of the Disciplinary Code.

Moreover, the fact that the ball was in play, or that the footballer subsequently took part in the same attacking move, does not in itself determine that, at the specific moment when the sanctioned conduct occurred, he was in a position to challenge for the ball. The referee’s report expressly states that the hair pull occurred “without the ball being contested between them,” a circumstance which, assessed together with the images, makes it possible to conclude that the action took place outside of an effective challenge for the ball.

Consequently, this Committee considers the application of Article 130.2 of the Disciplinary Code to be appropriate, proceeding to impose the suspension of two matches, the minimum provided for in the aforementioned article.

Regarding the allegations made by the Club concerning the conduct following the sending-off, this Committee considers that the facts recorded in the “Other incidents” section of the referee’s report constitute autonomous conduct, separate and distinct from that which led to the sending-off. The footage shows that, once sent off, he protested the referee’s decision, moving toward the referee in an aggressive manner and having to be restrained by his teammates.

Based on this, it is appropriate to impose a sanction of a two-match suspension, in application of article 127 of the Disciplinary Code, the minimum provided for in the aforementioned article.

By virtue of the foregoing, this Disciplinary Committee resolves:

To impose on Vinicius José de Oliveira do Nascimento the sanction of a two-match suspension pursuant to Article 130.2 of the Code

RFEF Disciplinary Committee, with the corresponding accessory fines

To impose on Vinicius José de Oliveira do Nascimento the sanction of a two-match suspension pursuant to article 127 of the Code

Disciplinary of the RFEF, with the corresponding accessory fines.

In this regard, reference may be made to the TAD Decision of 29 September 2017 (Case 302/2017), which stated that “when the aforementioned Article 27 of the RFEF Disciplinary Code states that refereeing decisions on facts related to play are ‘final and presumed true, save for manifest material error,’ it is allowing the principle of immutability (‘final’) enjoyed by the refereeing decision in favor of legal certainty, in this case, of the Laws of the Game, nevertheless to be mitigated when there is a ‘manifest material error,’ as a modality or subspecies of ‘material error,’ that is, where there exists, as the Constitutional Court has indicated when referring to this term in procedural laws (See Articles 214.3 of the Civil Procedure Act and 267.3 of the Organic Law of the Judiciary), a clear or obvious error, independently of any opinion, assessment, interpretation or legal classification that may be made.” (iii) Lastly, from all of the above it follows that, in order to challenge the truthfulness of the decisions recorded in the referee’s report, the appellant must provide the disciplinary body with appropriate and sufficient evidence to demonstrate the existence of “a manifest material error.” In this regard, it is also settled doctrine of the TAD that declares the full validity of video evidence as a suitable evidentiary instrument to rebut the content of the referee’s report. For its part, it is incumbent upon the Disciplinary Committee to review and assess the content of the recording in order to verify whether or not it corresponds to the appellant’s allegations. In short, only proof of a manifest material error would rebut the presumption of truthfulness enjoyed by the referee’s report and would make it possible to set aside the caution under appeal.

Third. None of these circumstances are present, in the opinion of this Disciplinary Committee, in the case before us, since the appealing Club does not provide any evidence whatsoever capable of disproving what is stated in the referee’s report.

On the contrary, the images are compatible with the referee's account, making the hair pull unequivocal, and the considerations regarding the position of the hand, the arrangement of the fingers, or the supposedly accidental nature of the contact do not allow a manifest material error to be established under the terms required by article 27.3 of the Disciplinary Code.

Moreover, the fact that the ball was in play, or that the footballer subsequently took part in the same attacking move, does not in itself determine that, at the specific moment when the sanctioned conduct occurred, he was in a position to challenge for the ball. The referee’s report expressly states that the hair pull occurred “without the ball being contested between them,” a circumstance which, assessed together with the images, makes it possible to conclude that the action took place outside of an effective challenge for the ball.

Consequently, this Committee considers the application of Article 130.2 of the Disciplinary Code to be appropriate, proceeding to impose the suspension of two matches, the minimum provided for in the aforementioned article.

Regarding the allegations made by the Club concerning the conduct following the sending-off, this Committee considers that the facts recorded in the “Other incidents” section of the referee’s report constitute autonomous conduct, separate and distinct from that which led to the sending-off. The footage shows that, once sent off, he protested the referee’s decision, moving toward the referee in an aggressive manner and having to be restrained by his teammates.
Based on this, it is appropriate to impose a sanction of a two-match suspension, in application of article 127 of the Disciplinary Code, the minimum provided for in the aforementioned article.
By virtue of the foregoing, this Disciplinary Committee resolves:
To impose on Vinicius José de Oliveira do Nascimento the sanction of a two-match suspension pursuant to Article 130.2 of the Code
RFEF Disciplinary Committee, with the corresponding accessory fines
To impose on Vinicius José de Oliveira do Nascimento the sanction of a two-match suspension pursuant to article 127 of the Code
Disciplinary of the RFEF, with the corresponding accessory fines.

articles.title: Barcelona already has a signing for El Clásico: it makes Tyler, the Creator's arrival official
articles.standfirst: The club announces the collaboration with the rapper and his brand GOLF WANG as part of its partnership with Spotify and takes over from Olivia Rodrigo
articles.summary: The club announces the collaboration with the rapper and his brand GOLF WANG as part of its partnership with Spotify and takes over from Olivia Rodrigo
articles.body:
Barcelona already has a musical star for the next Clásico . Tyler, the Creator will be the new face of the campaign the blaugrana club is preparing together with Spotify for the match against Real Madrid . "Welcome to the team, Tyler, The Creator," the club posted on its social media alongside a photograph of the American wearing Barça's colors.

The announcement also includes GOLF WANG , the artist's clothing brand, and confirms a choice that had been previously reported by RAC1 . The collaboration will have its big showcase next October 25 at Spotify Camp Nou , at 9:00 p.m., the kickoff time announced by Barcelona for hosting Real Madrid.

Football, music, and fashion come together once again around one of the most high-profile matches on the calendar. The blaugrana jersey has become one of the central pieces of the strategy designed together with Spotify, with a different leading figure at certain major occasions and a window that allows the club to reach audiences that go beyond football.

Tyler will be the ninth artist to take part in this initiative, launched with Drake in 2022. Then came Rosalía , The Rolling Stones , Karol G , Coldplay , Travis Scott , Ed Sheeran , and Olivia Rodrigo . Now comes a creator whose influence also extends to design, fashion, and urban culture .

His selection also revives the controversies that accompanied the early years of his career. Tyler Gregory Okonma , his real name, rose to fame as one of the driving forces behind the collective Odd Future . The lyrics from that period drew criticism for homophobic slurs and references to violence against women.

A past with varied episodes

The controversy had consequences in 2015, when the British Government barred him from entering the United Kingdom because of the content of his songs. The measure affected the performances he had planned in the country and placed his case within the debate over the limits of artistic provocation . The ban had already been lifted when he returned to London in 2019, so that prohibition remained linked to an earlier stage of his career.

Tyler now lands in the Clásico showcase with all that journey behind him. Barcelona and Spotify add to their collection of collaborations an artist with a visual identity of his own and a brand, GOLF WANG , that expands the proposal beyond music. The upcoming Barça-Madrid will also bear his signature.

articles.title: Former Barcelona president backtracks after brutal attack on Messi... but stops short of apologizing
articles.standfirst: "I sent Leo a message, and because I love him so much.. I went too far, I went too far"
articles.summary: "I sent Leo a message, and because I love him so much.. I went too far, I went too far"
articles.body:
Joan Gaspart, president of F.C. Barcelona from July 2000 to February 2003, wanted to clarify his brutal rant against Leo Messi on the podcast "Sólo Para Culés" .'

Messi should be careful. Barça is above him as a person

“I'm saying this out of the longstanding affection I have for a player I signed when he was 13 years old and I was the president of Barça.. He should be careful. Barça is above any individual,” was the much-discussed warning from the former Barça executive to Messi.

You can love Messi as much as I do, but you can't love Messi more than I do

Gaspart stated that "whoever the president is, Messi should come to say goodbye to Barça" , and hardened his stance by pointing out that "if Leo Messi comes to say goodbye and doesn't come because Laporta is the president, and comes on the day Laporta is no longer there, I wouldn't go to that tribute."

"Who does he think he is?" , he emphasized.

'Gaspart: "Am I going to apologize to Messi? I have never apologized to my children when I have reproached them for something"'

Days later Joan Gaspart wanted to clarify his words against Messi.

"Will I ask Messi for forgiveness? I have never asked my children for forgiveness when I have reproached them for something that I thought was best for them. You can love Messi as much as I do, but you cannot love Messi more than I do... I sent a message to Leo, and because I love him so much... I went too far, I went too far. Telling him "we love you very much, but Barça is bigger than you." It could have ended there," he replied to Jota Jordi on ¡Sólo para Culés.

articles.title: Arda Güler and Bernardo Silva ask for a place
articles.standfirst: Key figures in the comeback against Roma, they made their case to a Mourinho who once again opted for the Fede-Tchouaméni double pivot
articles.summary: Key figures in the comeback against Roma, they made their case to a Mourinho who once again opted for the Fede-Tchouaméni double pivot
articles.body:
The match against Roma showed that José Mourinho has a very clear idea of what his preferred midfield should look like. The Portuguese coach once again opted for the double pivot formed by Fede Valverde and Aurélien Tchouaméni . The result was disappointing, to the point that, in the first half, the player chosen to start the play for Madrid was neither the Uruguayan nor the Frenchman. That task fell to Thibaut Courtois, who, positioned between the center-backs, attempted up to 19 long passes, more than the two players theoretically responsible for giving meaning to Madrid's play .

It didn't work, neither in the first half nor at the start of the second, when Roma, through Malen , built a two-goal cushion ( 3-1 ) that seemed to put the match to bed. Seeing it slipping away, Mou overhauled his starting eleven, first bringing on Arda Güler (59th minute) and later Bernardo Silva (70'). The Turk's introduction moved Valverde to right-back, a position in which he had already been decisive against Villarreal . The Portuguese came on directly for Tchouaméni , forming a radically different double pivot from the one that started the match. With Arda and Bernardo, Madrid took control of the ball and ended up coming back thanks to two direct assists from the Turk, who also played an active role in Espí's goal .

The Valencian forward and Endrick were the other positive notes of Los Blancos' response. Both scored and brought a sense of danger to the Roman side's box, something that Vinicius was once again far from providing, despite starting barely a couple of hours after learning of his four-match suspension in the league. The Brazilian, along with Dumfries , was the first player withdrawn by his coach, in a radical tactical shake-up that ultimately proved worth three very valuable points at the Olimpico.

'Despite the team's radical change with the introductions of Arda and Bernardo, Mou resisted in the press conference any suggestion of continuing with that idea. And he did so emphatically. " If we start the way we finished, they'll put five past us. There are moments and moments. I had substitutions to make. They were going to get tired, the cards were going to come ," said the Madrid coach when asked about the change in script brought about by his substitutions in Rome. Statements that seem to reinforce his idea of opting for a more physical, less technical midfield in the upcoming matches, starting with Sunday's one against Sevilla. '

Moreover, one of the keys to that possible change of system lies in Fede Valverde's position . In the last two matches, the Uruguayan has had more influence on the game from full-back than in midfield. An old debate that has been circulating at Real Madrid for some time, despite the fact that the player openly opposed a change of position about a year ago, still with Xabi Alonso as Madrid's coach .

On Wednesday, Madrid's captain was less reluctant to the idea. "The important thing is to win, as the coach said. If things go well, you have to keep moving forward and I’m happy to keep getting minutes wherever it may be, I really enjoy playing, I had a lot of space to run down the wing and I’m grateful that the coach continues to trust me and I will give my all for the team," said Valverde, whose change of position had been ruled out by Mourinho before the Rome match. " If you have more than one Fede, you make him play at full-back, in midfield... But since we only have one Fede, seeing him at full-back is something very specific ," said the man from Setúbal.

A possible change of position for Fede would leave a spot open in midfield, opening the door to a midfield with more control and less muscle. The formula that worked in Rome, in a desperate situation that Madrid got out of thanks to Güler and Bernardo, two footballers pushing for a place at Madrid. The ball is in Mou's court .

articles.title: Lamine Yamal's Barcelona remains unstoppable and makes history with its ninth straight league win
articles.standfirst: Plenty of tension, plenty of goals, and plenty of controversy in another victory for Barça, which was decided after Facundo Bernal was sent off in the 54th minute
articles.summary: Plenty of tension, plenty of goals, and plenty of controversy in another victory for Barça, which was decided after Facundo Bernal was sent off in the 54th minute
articles.body:
Betis also came up short against this unstoppable Barça side, which has won all 12 official matches it has played. As expected, it was a game with everything in it, pitting two teams in top form against each other. High tension, plenty of goals, plenty of controversy, and a red card that ultimately decided the match in Flick’s team’s favor. Betis fans are particularly upset about a goal by Lo Celso that was disallowed—which would have tied the score at 2-2—due to a handball that occurred well before the goal was scored. Lamine once again made the difference, though he left La Cartuja to boos after playing a key role in Facundo Bernal’s ejection.

The toughest match so far for Flick’s team began to take shape before the 10-minute mark when Lamine Yamal pulled off a spectacular goal to dash Betis’ hopes. He received the ball on the wing, shook off Facundo Bernal with a cutback, and fired a pinpoint left-footed shot into the top corner of Valles’ net. Betis didn’t give up and managed to tie the game through Valentín Gómez, but Rodri before halftime, followed by Gabriel Jesus and Eric García, gave the league leaders the decisive lead. Pellegrini’s team briefly tied the game with a spectacular goal by Lo Celso, but it was ruled out via VAR due to a clear handball by Cucho Hernández at the start of the play. Controversy is sure to follow regarding the interpretation of the refereeing rules. Everyone sees it from their own perspective—the usual story. Facundo Bernal’s ejection ultimately sank Betis with half an hour of play remaining.

Flick’s team’s flawless start could be derailed by a grueling week of soccer, featuring away games against Betis and PSG and a high-stakes showdown at Camp Nou against Real Madrid. The first hurdle was a Champions League-caliber Betis side that hadn’t lost at La Cartuja in LaLiga since December 6, 2025—curiously, a 3-5 loss to Barça—in a span of 15 matches. And the test was passed, albeit controversially and successfully. Flick didn’t hold back and fielded a lineup that was essentially his first team, while Pellegrini rested some key players such as Isco, Natan, Deossa, and Antony.

Barça controlled possession from the start, and their dominance quickly translated into a lead with Lamine’s stunning goal into the top corner. On the other side, it was Abde who posed the home team’s greatest threat. The match unfolded exactly as the two players wearing the number 10 had hoped. And from a corner kick earned by the Moroccan, the equalizer came after a clearance fell to Fornals, who delivered a precise cross to the head of Valentín Gómez. The match opened up; there was no room for speculation at La Cartuja. Adeyemi had a chance to make it 1-2 after a great pass from Lamine, but Valles beat him in the one-on-one. Then it was Bellerín who had a chance to make it 2-1 off a pass from Fornals, but Joan García made a spectacular save.

The final minutes of the first half were nail-biting. Rodri made it 1-2 with a header off a corner kick taken by Fermín, leaving Valles half-way out of his goal. Betis didn’t let it get to them, and Lo Celso tied the game just a few minutes later with a great shot from outside the box. With the stands still going wild in celebration of the second equalizer, VAR alerted Ricardo de Burgos to a previous handball by Cucho Hernández, and the spectacular goal was disallowed—much to the despair of the entire Betis team—resulting in yellow cards for Diego Llorente and coach Pellegrini.

Barça’s start to the second half was just like the one in Istanbul in the Champions League. Thirty seconds in, Gabriel Jesus nearly scored off a pass from Adeyemi; then it was Fermín who forced Valles to make a spectacular save. Gabriel Jesus did score off a pass from Lamine, but the goal was called off for offside. The Brazilian found the net again a minute later off a pass from Lamine to make it 1-3. Betis protested a prior foul by Fermín. Before they had time to process the 1-3 score, it became 2-3 when Abde finished off a counterattack during which Barça claimed a foul on Fermín. That’s when things got heated: Valles roughly pulled Fermín to his feet while he was on the ground; Lamine stepped in to help his teammate; and Facundo Bernal ended the general scuffle with a head-to-head clash with Lamine that earned him a red card.

With the red card, the game was over

Down a man, Betis ran out of steam, and Barça immediately punished them with a fourth goal—a header by Eric García off a header from Cubarsí. That goal, which everyone could see was the definitive blow to the match, dampened the spirits, and the final 20 minutes seemed like a different game altogether. Both coaches began resting key players with an eye toward the Champions League, and Flick gave Raphinha a few minutes of playing time as he returned from injury while playing for Brazil. There was still time for Dani Olmo to score the fifth goal with a shot from outside the box. Eric García had to leave the game due to injury, which was the worst news for the Catalans. No one can stop this Barça. PSG and Real Madrid won’t make it easy for them in a few days.

articles.title: Barcelona ties Real Madrid's record of nine straight wins to start the league season
articles.standfirst: With nine consecutive victories at the start of the league season
articles.summary: With nine consecutive victories at the start of the league season
articles.body:
Barcelona keeps rolling. This Saturday, at La Cartuja, they secured their ninth consecutive league victory. A win that allows them to equal a new record, as they match Real Madrid's mark for the number of consecutive matches won at the start of the competition. The white club held the best record after stringing together nine straight wins in the 1968-1969 season.

The Merengue team was then coached by Miguel Muñoz and recorded those nine consecutive victories before drawing nil-nil on matchday ten against Pontevedra. With the win in Seville, Barcelona equals this record and will now have the opportunity to surpass it in the next round. Moreover, it so happens that their opponent will be Real Madrid, in the Clásico to be played at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday the 25th.

Hansi Flick's team is in extraordinary form. They have shown it since the start of the competition this season. To the league victories, we must also add the two wins they have achieved in the Champions League against Feyenoord and Galatasaray. Their extraordinary attacking power has been key to winning every match they have played.

Now they face two very complicated consecutive matches. The first will be next Tuesday against PSG, in the Champions League. The Blaugrana will visit the home ground of the current European champions and will have many difficulties maintaining their streak against Luis Enrique's team . articles.standfirst: The Catalan will also not be in the Clásico and the Frenchman is doubtful
articles.summary: The Catalan will also not be in the Clásico and the Frenchman is doubtful
articles.body:
Barcelona lose Eric García and Koundé for Tuesday's match against PSG , corresponding to the third matchday of the Champions group stage. In fact, the Catalan will be out for around a month and, therefore, will also miss the Clásico . For his part, the Frenchman is a doubt for Sunday's clash against Real Madrid at Spotify Camp Nou .

The team landed in Barcelona early in the afternoon, after the problems they had returning from Seville due to the rain , and both players went directly to undergo medical tests. In the case of Eric García , the examinations revealed that he is suffering from a muscle injury to the rectus femoris of his right thigh, so the recovery time will be between three and four weeks. Therefore, he will also be unavailable for next Sunday’s match against Real Madrid , in the first Clásico of the season.

Koundé , for his part, was visibly limping as he got off the plane. Tests revealed that he is suffering from a sprain in his left ankle. He will not be available on Tuesday at the Parc des Princes , but he is doubtful for the LaLiga match against Los Blancos. "His recovery will determine his availability against Real Madrid ," read the statement issued by the club shortly before 6:00 p.m.

In the case of Gerard Martín, who had to be substituted at halftime after being stepped on, it was not necessary to carry out medical tests. Everything therefore points to it being only a knock, and he should be available for the match against PSG . That said, given the limited recovery time, it remains to be seen whether the Catalan will be one hundred percent.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal arrives unleashed for "his" big week: PSG and Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: The Catalan, moreover, rises to the occasion on prestigious stages
articles.summary: The Catalan, moreover, rises to the occasion on prestigious stages
articles.body:
If Lamine Yamal was already tipped to be one of the standout protagonists of next week at Barcelona , his latest performances in the second half of the clash against Galatasaray and the showdown at La Cartuja have only multiplied expectations. The young winger heads into one of the most demanding stretches of the season, with PSG and Real Madrid , in extraordinary form, producing moves, dribbles and shots that seem straight out of a video game and brought directly onto the pitch.

Moreover, the footballer from Rocafonda has never hidden that the biggest stages represent a special motivation for him. And if there are two opponents capable of bringing out his competitiveness to the fullest, those are PSG and Real Madrid .

Barcelona faces one of the most important weeks of the season. Not so much because of the definitive nature of the results, since there is still a long way to go in both the Champions and LaLiga, but because of the magnitude of the challenges ahead. The blaugrana side will take on PSG this Tuesday in a match that will serve to gauge their European ambitions against one of the major contenders for the title. On Sunday, moreover, the Clásico will arrive, an opportunity to make a statement in the regular championship. Two matches of maximum demand in which the inspiration of Lamine Yamal could prove decisive.

And the winger arrives especially motivated. Despite having accumulated a significant number of minutes during the international break, Hansi Flick has continued to rely on him in Barcelona 's matches. The physical wear and tear could have raised doubts, but his latest performances have shown that he remains a crucial footballer and that he does not need to rest or be rotated.

Against Galatasaray , in the second half, Lamine became the standout star of the match. He provided two assists and was involved in the move that led to Barça’s fourth goal. Beyond his statistics, one of the actions that drew much of the attention was a dribble of enormous technical difficulty that quickly went viral around the world.

"If he had already shown signs of his exceptional quality against the Turkish side, on Saturday, against Betis , he once again put on a masterclass. His goal in the 10th minute was a true exhibition: a left-footed shot from the edge of the area, with an exquisite trademark curl. But his performance was not limited to the goal. Lamine also assisted Gabriel Jesus and produced several individual plays in which he once again displayed his full repertoire.

To his technical qualities is added, moreover, a competitive personality that grows the greater the challenge. Lamine Yamal enjoys the most demanding matches and does not shy away from responsibility when the spotlight is focused on him.

For all these reasons, the footballer from Rocafonda faces the week on a high and at a particularly exciting moment. PSG and Real Madrid represent two top-level tests to see just how far this Barcelona can go. Lamine arrives flying, with confidence, footballing arguments, and a desire to keep proving his strong candidacy for the Ballon d'Or .

articles.title: Güler clears the way for Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: The Turkish player stole the show with his spectacular goal and a play leading up to it with Peque that Busquets didn't interpret as a foul. Mbappé, with a two-goal performance, and Diomande rounded out the scoring against an outraged Sevilla
articles.summary: The Turkish player stole the show with his spectacular goal and a play leading up to it with Peque that Busquets didn't interpret as a foul. Mbappé, with a two-goal performance, and Diomande rounded out the scoring against an outraged Sevilla
articles.body:
Real Madrid came out on top in the match leading up to El Clásico , showing improved play and confidence, with Güler at the heart of it all. The Turkish player was instrumental in breaking the deadlock with a spectacular goal just minutes after a play involving Peque in which a foul was called. Arda risked a red card, it’s true, but so did the fact that he improved Real Madrid’s play in the midfield. Madrid was also more compact with Valverde on one wing and Diomande on the other. Vinicius played better—that’s a fact. Sevilla competed with pride, fueled by indignation. They played well, but the referees’ calls went against them.

A suspension and a dozen games sent Madrid back to where they were a year ago. Mourinho reviewed data and statistics to position Valverde on the right wing and Güler in the center of the field for the penultimate warm-up match before the Camp Nou. That decision cost Xabi his first clash with the squad, and after two adjustments to win two tough matches (against Villarreal and Roma), the Uruguayan moved to the wing, with Trent and Dumfries available. In short, it wasn’t a desperate move. Fede did it all: fullback, central midfielder, and winger.

His was the first clear chance of a match that began with a protest. Ten minutes of chants against Tebas, Laporta, Negreira, and the Federation. Anyway, shortly after the protest ended, Bellingham broke through on the right, played a pass back, and Valverde popped up at the edge of the box to unleash a right-footed shot. Mbappé cleared it with his back. Sevilla, arriving at the Bernabéu sharing the team’s anger toward the referees (and rightly so), struggled early on, and just when they were starting to feel more comfortable in the match, their frustration only grew. Without Isaac Romero, Luis García deployed Robbie Ure as the striker and Peque behind him in a dual role: to cut into the spaces between the lines and to mark Güler. That’s when he grabbed Arda during a counterattack, and the Turkish player broke free. Peque fell to the ground, apparently after being elbowed. The Sevillians protested, but Cuadra Fernández in the VAR booth apparently couldn’t find any clear and obvious footage showing that the foul had occurred. Although it seemed even more obvious than Vinicius’s hair-pulling incident. To make matters worse, seven minutes later, Diomande—generous with and without the ball—played it back from his wing, and Arda, on the first touch, curled a left-footed shot into the opposite top corner.

Sevilla closed ranks before play resumed. Well-organized, they had found good ways to break free from Madrid’s pressure and sought to stay in the game. They struggled because, with the lead, Madrid’s strengths came to the fore. Endrick looked to get behind the defense with his weaker foot, Bellingham made runs into the box, and Güler showcased his passing ability. Take, for example, a pass to Valverde, which the Uruguayan sent into the box but failed to connect with Mbappé. The Frenchman was saving his moment of brilliance. Sevilla looked to counter; Ure battled with Konaté—including some pulling—but Courtois made the save, played it out wide, the ball reached the edge of the box, Bellingham backheeled it, and Kylian scored a stunning goal: a spin, a sharp cutback past Salas, a one-two against Odysseas, and into the net. The Sevilla fans called for a foul beforehand, just like Cucho’s handball the day before. No luck there. Sevilla tried to pull one back before halftime, but Agoume’s hard shot was met by a miraculous save from Courtois. Decisive.

Luis García made a change on the right wing after the break, bringing on Ejuke for Vargas. The fans’ complaints about the refereeing didn’t let up, even though there was a sense in the air that this time there was no reason for them. Quite the opposite, in fact. Diomande capitalized on a mistake by Juan Iglesias and a give-and-go in midfield that allowed him to break free toward the edge of the box. He lacked finesse on the final touch in both plays, while the newly substituted Ejuke was giving Cucurella a hard time. Juan Iglesias made a run down that flank, chipping the ball to the far post where Correia volleyed it. Valverde made a providential save, keeping the lead intact to seal the victory. It came on a deep pass from Diomande to Mbappé, which the Frenchman turned into a penalty by cutting in behind Castrín. Of course. Kylian changed his approach and executed a perfect Panenka. And just as in the first half, Courtois stepped up again to secure the lead. Sevilla made a good run to the edge of the box, Fofana took a shot, and the Belgian made the save.

Mourinho made some smart substitutions

Güler left the field to a standing ovation from the crowd. Bernardo and Brahim—who hadn’t played since the match against Inter—got some playing time. The fact is, Real Madrid’s intensity dropped a bit, and Sevilla took advantage of it. Manu Bueno gave a warning sign after a rehearsed free kick—the same player who capitalized on a turnover by Mbappé to score a great goal, a low shot with his left foot. He barely had time to enjoy it, because Diomande sealed the deal with another great goal, breaking from the left and unleashing a powerful right-footed strike. That was the end of a match that Sevilla will rightly complain about—every refereeing decision went against them. Controversy aside, Madrid improved in their play, their intent, and their tactical variety. They looked more compact. It remains to be seen whether this version of the team will be enough to stop Barça.

articles.title: Mbappé: “I’ve shown time and again that I can do stupid things"
articles.standfirst: The forward, chosen as the Onze d’Or best player of the 2025-26 season, opens up in an interview in his most personal side
articles.summary: The forward, chosen as the Onze d’Or best player of the 2025-26 season, opens up in an interview in his most personal side
articles.body:
K ylian Mbappé has been chosen as the Onze d’Or, the award for the best footballer of the season that the French magazine Onze Mondial has granted since 1976 through the vote of its readers, beating Joao Neves and Kvaratskhelia . In the interview afterward, the Real Madrid forward showed his most human side and began by dismantling the myth of the perfect boy. “Anyone who thinks I’m perfect clearly doesn’t have a television!” , he joked. “I’ve shown time and again that I can do stupid things. And I’m okay with that. I think that’s fine too.”

The Frenchman argued that the screen distorts people's perception of him: “No one really knows you through television. That’s why sometimes there are analyses that are out of step with reality” . And he illustrated it with an example: “If you ask me to judge an actor whose films I’ve only seen, I can give an opinion completely opposite to what the person is really like. That’s why I don’t pass judgment, because I have the experience of going to the other side of the screen and I know what it’s like”.

Far from lowering the ambition that has led him to declare himself the best in the world, a phrase that is not always understood in France, Mbappé defended it as a tool. “I understand everything. I know the history and culture of my country, so I know what it can provoke when I say things like that” , he admitted. “When I say it, it’s because I think it and because it is a motivation. To do great things, you can’t go out onto the field thinking that others can do it better than you. That would be setting a limit for yourself”.

To say that I am the best? I know what it can cause when I say things like that, I think it and it is a motivation

The Frenchman claimed doubt as the driving force behind his longevity at the elite level. “You don’t become a player with such a lasting presence over time if you don’t think, if you don’t reflect, if you don’t doubt,” he said. “Doubt is very important, because it allows you to improve yourself, not to rest on your laurels. I constantly reflect on what I can do, what I have done, what I am doing” . Speaking about his career, more than a decade after his debut, he did not hesitate in the interview: “A ten. The main thing I take away is not the goals or the titles, but that in these ten or eleven years I haven’t been bored for a single year. I have never pulled the handbrake.”

"True to his idea that a footballer is won over by talking to him about football, Mbappé defined his next goal: to understand the game on a deeper level. “I want to truly understand the moments of a match, of a season, of a play. To have more control over what I do, to leave less room for the unknown,” he explained. Not at the expense of his essence, of course: “You have to leave room for creativity and instinct, because they are part of my game, and that is something I must never lose.”

On how he handles the pressure of millions of people, the striker emphasized the perspective that the years have given him. “It’s difficult if you take it personally, and I used to take it that way when I was younger” , he admitted. “Today I’m 27 years old, I have distance, and I understand that sometimes there are people who aren’t looking to analyze and that’s just how it is. The most important thing is to be in tune with your values, with your principles, with the message you want to send.” And he summed up his character in one image: “I’m a guy who adapts. More than a chameleon, a child of the world” .

He also had words for those who dream of becoming like him. “I tell all those kids that wanting to be me is setting a limit for yourself, and the goal of dreaming is not to set limits for yourself ,” he said. “If they can dream of being more than me, they shouldn’t hold back!” The forward also brushed aside any complaint about the burdens of fame: “I have always felt privileged . It would seem out of place to me, in the world we live in, to complain about being Kylian”.

Asked whether he is happy, Mbappé replied without qualification. “Of course I’m a happy man. I’ve had the life I always wanted to have. I always wanted to be a footballer, and I’ve fulfilled my dream of playing in the best competitions every weekend,” he concluded. “What would I need to be happier? Nothing. In life I’m not someone who always seeks to have more. At work, yes, but in life, no. You have to know how to be content with what you have.”

articles.summary: None of the 23 cameras set up at the Bernabéu had "sufficient detail" to provide "conclusive evidence"
articles.body:
The controversy sparked by Arda Güler's elbow to Peque during the first half of Real Madrid-Sevilla with the score at 0-0, which has outraged Sevilla supporters who believe the Turk should have been sent off, has pointed directly to the VAR room and the television production, produced since last season by Global Futbol Production (GFP).

Sources from LaLiga, contacted by this newspaper, have explained that the reason there is no clear shot of the play despite 23 being used for the match broadcast is that only the wider-angle ones—the endline camera, the Skycam, and the one intended for offsides—captured the image.

It was not a production error, simply that it does not exist. And the signal that reaches the television truck that broadcasts the images to every home, they say, is the same one received by Cuadra Fernández's team, the one responsible for VAR in the match at the Bernabéu.

Meanwhile, other sources from the Technical Committee of Referees (CTA) pointed out that "of the multiple cameras at the match, not all are suitable for VAR. The action takes place behind the referee’s back, in an off-the-ball area. The cameras were not focused there, only those with a very wide shot. As has been seen, the action appears, but there is no detail".

And they add that "it is not clear whether he hits him with the shoulder, with the elbow, with the hand, in the face... It cannot be seen. And since there is no evidence, it cannot be intervened in. On the field it was not penalized and the VAR, without conclusive proof, cannot do anything".

GFP took over from Mediapro last year. It is a joint venture formed by HBS (on the production side) and the Italian technology company NVP (on the technical services side). It signed a five-season deal with LaLiga, through 29/30.

articles.title: Who is Gabriel Wesseh? The 18-year-old American talent on Barcelona’s radar
articles.standfirst: An 18-year-old winger who currently plays for Norwegian side Fredrikstad
articles.summary: An 18-year-old winger who currently plays for Norwegian side Fredrikstad
articles.body:
Norwegian journalist Erlend Borren Kristoffersen, a reporter for TV 2 Sporten, caused a stir on X after claiming that Barcelona are closely monitoring Gabriel Wesseh, an 18-year-old American winger who currently plays for Norwegian side Fredrikstad.

“Barcelona have sent scouts to the stands for two matches to watch him play,” the Norwegian journalist said. According to his information, Barça are not the only club interested in Wesseh, although they are the biggest name in the race.

Benfica and Club Brugge, two clubs known for identifying and investing in young talent before selling players for significant profits, are also reportedly interested in the youngster, who is under contract with Fredrikstad until 2030.

Scouting reports highlight Wesseh’s pace, dribbling ability and versatility, with the winger capable of playing on either flank. He previously spent time in the Atlanta and Philadelphia academies during the early stages of his career in the United States.

Wesseh has already made his debut for the United States U-19 team and is regarded as one of the promising players of his USMNT generation. For now, he will remain in Norway’s top flight, although a move to a bigger European club could become a reality next season.

articles.title: What's happening with Trent Alexander-Arnold at Real Madrid? "It's not working"
articles.standfirst: Trent Alexander-Arnold's situation at Real Madrid has taken an unexpected turn this season
articles.summary: Trent Alexander-Arnold's situation at Real Madrid has taken an unexpected turn this season
articles.body:
Trent Alexander-Arnold's arrival at Real Madrid in the summer of 2025 was presented as one of the most exciting moves in the European market . The full-back arrived from Liverpool with the status of a global star and with the mission of dominating the right flank of the white side for the next decade . However, the reality the England international has encountered in the Spanish capital differs greatly from the initial expectations generated after his free transfer.

As the weeks have gone by, his impact on the team has gradually lost strength to the point of becoming a regular on the bench . Recent reports suggest that his performances have failed to convince the coaching staff and that his role within the current squad has been drastically reduced. This loss of status has set off alarm bells at the club and sparked a debate over his definitive fit in Real Madrid's tactical setup.

The British defender's lack of minutes is not a matter of chance, but rather the reflection of a series of shortcomings that have come to light in the demanding dynamics of Spanish competition . Various specialized media outlets, with an in-depth analysis published by The Athletic, detail that Trent's main problems lie in his defensive weaknesses, an aspect that at Real Madrid is non-negotiable, especially in the most demanding matches.

The Englishman's defensive weaknesses

The demanding tactical rigor imposed by José Mourinho at the Santiago Bernabéu has brought to light the British full-back's defensive shortcomings . Although his attacking talent and the quality of his ball striking are undeniable, his lapses in concentration when marking and his struggles in one-on-one defensive duels have weighed too heavily in the coaching staff's assessments.

In this regard, the article "Trent Alexander-Arnold's adventure at Real Madrid is not working out", produced by The Athletic, points out that these defensive shortcomings have caused him to lose ground alarmingly in the team's rotation . The full-back has played only a handful of matches and has been strung together on the bench in consecutive games, seeing how other players are getting the better of him in a key position for the stability of the Merengue block.

Internal competition at Real Madrid

"Trent's situation has worsened even further due to the emergence of tactical alternatives within the squad itself . In the early stages of the campaign, summer signing Denzel Dumfries enjoyed the confidence of the Portuguese coach, but the situation has taken a radical turn with a surprising tactical variation.

And according to outlets such as Tribuna, the Uruguayan Federico Valverde has established himself in an unexpected transformation as the starting right-back . The versatility, physical output, and defensive reliability of the Charrúa have fully convinced Mourinho, pushing the former Liverpool player into the background ahead of the most important fixtures of the season.

The salary factor and the exit rumors

Against this backdrop of ostracism, rumors of a possible departure from the white club have not been long in appearing in the international sports press . Various transfer market portals have recently pointed to an alleged interest from major Premier League clubs, noting that Chelsea would be closely monitoring his situation in the event of a hypothetical escape route.

However, those same reports clarify that an immediate departure from Real Madrid is extremely complex in the short term . The main obstacle lies in the player's high financial demands and in a long-term contract that runs until 2031, figures that complicate any departure deal unless the financial positions between the parties become more flexible .

The club's stance and the future

"Despite the rumors placing him on the way out and the links with British teams such as the Stamford Bridge side—where outlets like OneFootball have assessed market scenarios—, Real Madrid's board maintains a stance of prudence and calm regarding the player's future .

Sources close to the merengue club recall that the project with Alexander-Arnold is long-term and that the player has the necessary room to definitively adapt to Spanish football . The challenge for the 28-year-old full-back now is to absorb Mourinho's defensive demands and regain confidence in training to reverse a situation that currently appears delicate.

articles.title: They reveal an unmissable anecdote about Ronaldinho's "initiation" of Messi at Barça: "With a stolen helmet"
articles.standfirst: The former Mexican footballer recounts on "La Granja VIP" an anecdote that, according to him, the Brazilian told him during his time at Querétaro. A story from the Argentine's early years at Barcelona
articles.summary: The former Mexican footballer recounts on "La Granja VIP" an anecdote that, according to him, the Brazilian told him during his time at Querétaro. A story from the Argentine's early years at Barcelona
articles.body:
'Before becoming the great benchmark of Barcelona , Leo Messi was the newcomer to a dressing room ruled by Ronaldinho . The Brazilian welcomed him and helped him find his place among the stars. From that time together, there are also stories off the pitch. One of them has just come to light through Mario "El Mono" Osuna , who shared a team with the Brazilian at Querétaro .'

'During a conversation about football on the program " La Granja VIP ", the former Mexican player recalled an alleged initiation prank on the Argentine. According to his account, Ronaldinho had told him that several Barça footballers went out partying one night and ended up putting a motorcycle helmet on Messi that they had taken from outside the venue.'

Osuna said that the "helmet had been stolen " and that the Argentine wore it during the outing. This is a second-hand version: the Mexican recounts what, according to him, Ronaldinho told him. The account does not specify when it happened or which other players took part.

The anecdote turns the spotlight back on a Messi who was still making his way. The young La Masia player lived alongside established footballers and had Ronaldinho as his main role model. The Brazilian was the team's star; the Argentine was beginning to show the talent that would end up changing the club's history.

The pass that started it all

The image that best explains that connection is on the pitch. Messi's first official goal with Barcelona came after an assist from Ronaldinho: a chipped ball over the Albacete defense that the Argentine finished with a lob.

As time went by, that play took on a special meaning. The footballer leading Barça had set up the ball for the first goal of the one who would end up taking over from him. The celebration, with Messi on the Brazilian's back, left behind a photograph inseparable from their beginnings.

His relationship was also built in the day-to-day life of the dressing room . Ronaldinho accompanied the breakthrough of a teammate who still had to earn his place and seemed to quickly sense how far he could go.

' Maxi López , who played with both of them at Barcelona , said that the Brazilian made a confession to him about that young player: "This kid is better than me." An especially striking assessment because it came from a Ronaldinho who was at the top.'

articles.title: Courtois, last-minute absence for the Clásico
articles.standfirst: The Real Madrid goalkeeper is suffering from a bout of flu
articles.summary: The Real Madrid goalkeeper is suffering from a bout of flu
articles.body:
Real Madrid has suffered a major setback. The white club announced this Sunday that Courtois will be out for tonight's Clásico against Barcelona at Spotify Camp Nou.

The Belgian will not be part of the match due to a flu-like illness that prevents him from being in optimal condition to compete in the first Clásico of this season, corresponding to the tenth matchday of LaLiga.

Real Madrid will therefore have to change goalkeepers, and it will be Andriy Lunin who takes to the pitch at the blaugrana stadium to play the match. Illia Voloshyn, the Ukrainian goalkeeper for Real Madrid C, comes into the squad following Courtois's absence.

This setback is not new. With today's, it will be the third match he has missed due to flu or flu-related gastroenteritis. The same thing happened to him last season, in November, and once again in 2023. In 2019 he missed another one with stomach problems . In total he has missed 108 matches through injury, serious or minor like tonight's, since he signed for Real Madrid in 2018.

But it will be the first match Courtois will miss this season since he had played in the first nine league rounds. His absence is a major setback for Mourinho's team in a very important match if they want to close in on Barça at the top of the table

articles.title: Kylian Mbappé Leads Real Madrid to 2-1 Victory Over Barcelona in Thrilling El Clasico
articles.standfirst: The Frenchman became the hero in the 88th minute to seal a thrilling match at Camp Nou
articles.summary: The Frenchman became the hero in the 88th minute to seal a thrilling match at Camp Nou
articles.body:
Two goals from Kylian Mbappe , one off a rebound and the other a decisive one in the 88th minute, ended Barça's unbeaten run , as they were always chasing the game and ended up losing (1-2) in their worst match in a long time.

Jose Mourinho , Real Madrid's manager, read the course of the match to perfection and short-circuited Barça, who were never at their level, and conquered Camp Nou, a stage where the Blaugrana had strung together 23 victories since May 2025 .

Barça started better, but the control effect faded in barely five minutes. Real Madrid allowed Barça’s center-backs to build from the back, and that is where Mourinho’s team found its vein, with Gerard Martín as the Achilles’ heel, only Cubarsí created, and midfielders Rodri and Pedri did not show up.

Real Madrid surprised with Bernardo Silva's inclusion in midfield. He fielded four of the new signings, gave Guler freedom, and entrusted everything to the work of Bellingham , the pace of Mbappe , and the dribbling of Diomande .

But the match started out thick, and in the game of mistakes, Madrid felt at home and, after a moment of doubt from Pedri, Arda Guler issued the first warning in the 5th minute. Both teams felt more comfortable winning the ball back and attacking directly, a bad sign for Barça in this change of roles.

Without any combination play, with an unrecognizable Pedri, and with the few appearances of Lamine Yamal and the occasional spark from Raphinha, Gordon capitalized on the home side's attacking moves. In fact, all the play flowed down that flank, where Arda Guler was Mourinho's side's beacon.

The Turk appeared in the 18th minute, with a good shot parried away by Joan Garcia, and from then on Barça, with Raphinha as the main figure, the Blaugrana, although lacking creativity, did threaten more, although the match was where Mourinho wanted it.

Raphinha , in the 22nd minute, after a move by Pedri ; the Brazilian again in a play involving Gordon (24) and once more LALIGA’s top scorer (33) with a shot just inside the post suggested that Barça could take the lead, but nothing could have been further from what actually happened.

Real Madrid had studied every twist in the script of the movie, and when after half an hour Xavi Espart had to come off at right-back, they saw the sky open up and Barça started to show its seams.

With Espart, Joao Cancelo injured, he played on the right and Balde came on down the left. Diomande and Cucurella smelled blood and, in a fortunate play, an action by Diomande fell to the feet of Gerard Martín ; his clearance deflected off Mbappé , who just happened to be there, and the ball ended up in Joan Garcia 's net in the 41st minute (0-1).

Before the break, Barça could have equalized in a move by Lamine , who shot wide when through alone against Lunin , and Diomande could also have extended his team's lead, with a shot into the side netting in added time.

'The "Flick effect" didn't work'

Flick's effect to change the match at halftime did not appear, and his team played with more risk, but without accuracy. On the Madrid side, Bellingham emerged as the standout player.

In the 50th minute, the Englishman did not choose well in a two-on-one alongside Mbappé, with Gerard Martín as the only defender. And from then on, Barça tried to inject pace into the match and Madrid tried to kill it off with some move by the Frenchman.

The first good move by Pedri during the match changed the outlook for his side. He set up Raphinha with a through pass, and the Brazilian beat Lunin with a low cross-shot in the 61st minute (1-1).

The equalizer seemed to change everything, but that was not the case. The match opened up, Real Madrid was already having doubts, although Guler still had a good chance to beat Joan Garcia . Without pause, in the next play, Lunin saved his team with a huge stop from a header by Gerard Martín (min. 66).

The final quarter of an hour was a Barça siege, but Real Madrid always looked dangerous on one of Mbappe 's runs. And that is how the match was decided, with an excellent move by Camavinga , who gifted the goal to his compatriot to decide the game in the 88th minute (1-2).

The victory leaves the league more tightly packed, with Barça as leader, but with Atlético de Madrid two points behind and Real Madrid, in third, three points back.

2 - Real Madrid: Lunin; Valverde (Dumfries, min. 62), Konaté, Huijsen, Cucurella; Tchouaméni, Bernardo Silva (Camavinga, min. 80), Bellingham, Güler (Alexander Arnold, min. 90+4), Diomande (Espí, min. 90+4); and Mbappe.

Goals: 0-1, 41st minute: Mbappe. 1-1, 61st minute: Raphinha. 1-2, 88th minute: Mbappe.

Referee: Juan Martínez Munuera (Valencian Committee). He booked Tchouaméni (min. 46), Gordon (min. 84), Huijsen (min. 90+2), Balde (min. 90+7) and Adeyemi (min. 90+7).

'The "Flick effect" didn't work'
Flick's effect to change the match at halftime did not appear, and his team played with more risk, but without accuracy. On the Madrid side, Bellingham emerged as the standout player.

In the 50th minute, the Englishman did not choose well in a two-on-one alongside Mbappé, with Gerard Martín as the only defender. And from then on, Barça tried to inject pace into the match and Madrid tried to kill it off with some move by the Frenchman.
The first good move by Pedri during the match changed the outlook for his side. He set up Raphinha with a through pass, and the Brazilian beat Lunin with a low cross-shot in the 61st minute (1-1).

The equalizer seemed to change everything, but that was not the case. The match opened up, Real Madrid was already having doubts, although Guler still had a good chance to beat Joan Garcia . Without pause, in the next play, Lunin saved his team with a huge stop from a header by Gerard Martín (min. 66).

The final quarter of an hour was a Barça siege, but Real Madrid always looked dangerous on one of Mbappe 's runs. And that is how the match was decided, with an excellent move by Camavinga , who gifted the goal to his compatriot to decide the game in the 88th minute (1-2).
The victory leaves the league more tightly packed, with Barça as leader, but with Atlético de Madrid two points behind and Real Madrid, in third, three points back.

articles.title: Vinicius's two messages to Barça after the Clásico
articles.standfirst: The Brazilian, absent due to suspension, reacted to Real Madrid's victory at Camp Nou with four laughing emojis and a message that did not go unnoticed
articles.summary: The Brazilian, absent due to suspension, reacted to Real Madrid's victory at Camp Nou with four laughing emojis and a message that did not go unnoticed
articles.body:
Real Madrid stormed the Spotify Camp Nou (1-2), and Vinicius did not miss the chance to send a message after the Whites' victory. Although he could not be on the pitch due to suspension, the Brazilian made himself noticed on social media with a reaction that did not go unnoticed .

Shortly after Madrid's victory, the forward shared the result in an Instagram story accompanied by four laughing emojis . The Brazilian, who missed the match after receiving a four-game suspension for his assault on Saliba in the clash against Villarreal, joined in the celebration of a Real Madrid side that earned three golden points to climb aboard the LaLiga train.

In addition, the Brazilian also commented on a post in which he appeared pointing to the club's 15 Champions League titles . Two gestures with which he wanted to stand up for Madrid after an immensely valuable victory at the home of their eternal rival. However, despite the great Madrid victory... the match leaves him in the spotlight after a huge performance from Diomande, who worked as hard as anyone and created a lot of danger . An example that you can be decisive going forward and help in defense.

articles.title: An absolute mess: How a Mao Zedong meme got Kylian Mbappé and Real Madrid banned from Chinese TV
articles.standfirst: He replaced Mbappé's name with the Chinese expression "chá wú cǐ rén", which means "there is no such person" or "person not found"
articles.summary: He replaced Mbappé's name with the Chinese expression "chá wú cǐ rén", which means "there is no such person" or "person not found"
articles.body:
The Chinese sports portal Dongqiudi replaced the name of Kylian Mbappé with the expression "no such person exists" in the 2026 Ballon d'Or standings, in which the Real Madrid forward finished second, following the controversy over some remarks about a "meme" comparing him to Mao Zedong .

In the list published this Tuesday, the outlet identified the winner, England's Harry Kane, and the third-place finisher, Spain's Lamine Yamal, but replaced the Frenchman's name with the Chinese expression "chá wú cǐ rén," which means "no such person exists" or "person not found ".

Dongqiudi published a black-and-white photograph of Mbappé... as if he had died

Dongqiudi, one of China’s leading digital platforms specializing in football, also published a black-and-white photograph of Mbappé , a visual treatment that on Chinese social media is usually associated with images of deceased people .

On Monday, the portal had released a statement in which it described the footballer's remarks as "unacceptable" and stated that it would not translate them because it considered them harmful to the feelings of fans and the Chinese people.

The controversy began after Mbappé said in an interview that one of the "memes" he found most amusing showed his face over that of a "Chinese dictator," although he did not expressly mention Mao.

The controversy caused the termination this Tuesday of Mbappé's commercial agreements with the Chinese companies Dongpeng, Mengniu, and Milkground, while China's Foreign Ministry warned that words and actions that "hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will be rejected by all sectors of society."

State broadcaster CCTV suspended LaLiga broadcasts, according to The Paper citing sources from the public radio and television network, while the platform Xiaohongshu (RedNote) prevents users from following the footballer's account, as EFE was able to verify, and announced the removal of content related to him, although it clarified that its commercial collaboration had ended in 2024
